title: fix(cron): exclude interruptions from failure auto-disable
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart or operator cancellation could push an automation over its consecutive-failure threshold and disable it, even though the interruption was not a job failure.

## User Impact

Recurring automations keep their existing failure streak and remain enabled after an interruption. Interruption history remains visible. Interrupted one-shots remain disabled to avoid replaying work whose side effects are uncertain. Existing disabled automations are not automatically re-enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup recovery counted abandoned executions as failures and could queue auto-disable or repair notifications. Normal finalization also counted explicitly aborted runs. Remove that startup failure machinery and use the existing cancellation classification to exclude aborted outcomes from failure streaks, auto-disable, and failure notifications. Genuine timeouts and job failures keep the existing policy. Error scheduling also stays unchanged: cancellation completion anchors backoff using the preserved count (including the existing minimum floor at zero). This keeps finalization and maintenance consistent without adding stored classification fields. No schema, stored-format, or configuration changes.

## Evidence

The five new regression cases failed before the fix (failure count increments and unintended disablement) and pass afterward. Four focused files passed: `service/run-recovery.test.ts`, `service/timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts`, `service/startup-run-repair.auto-disable.test.ts`, and `service.failure-repair.test.ts` — 66 tests, 128.40s total including cold worker preparation/transforms. After the review adjustment, recovery passed again and the final outcome/maintenance file passed all 20 tests (47.03s including transforms). Existing permanent-error, transient retry, failure-repair, and one-shot cancellation coverage remained green.

Changed-file formatting, syntax/boundary lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Production delta: 14 lines added, 48 removed (net −34); obsolete restart-as-failure notification tests were removed in favor of recovery-boundary proof. Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) identified inconsistent backoff handling; restored the existing policy and added recovery/maintenance assertions. Revised review is clean through P2. Broad validation belongs to PR CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease or local full suite/build/typecheck was run. This is a correctness fix with fewer production lines, not a latency optimization; no performance claim or benchmark.

PR CI found four stale counter assertions in `src/cron/store/run-receipt-delivery.test.ts`. Reproduced all four locally, updated them to assert unchanged absent failure count and no auto-disable reason while preserving one-shot no-replay checks, and reran only that file: 7/7 pass (39.40s including transforms). Independent review of the test-only follow-up is clean. No CI rerun was requested; the corrective commit triggers new exact-head CI.

Automated review identified that webhook-delivery cancellation could overwrite an already completed core failure with an aborted classification. The outcome mapper now preserves the completed failure and retains cancellation separately in delivery diagnostics. Two real cron/webhook-path cases reproduced the hidden failure counts; final due-run cases verify ordinary failure alerting and the tenth-failure auto-disable. The delivery file passes 17/17 (14.32s including transforms, 17.32s wrapper), and the existing interruption mapper file passes 6/6. Independent review of this follow-up is clean. Total focused coverage: 96 tests across seven files.

Final head `5f890e7f7665d983c29b26d027122d91531689b5` passed PR CI run [38707093528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38707093528), including every changed-code test job and the aggregate gate. All required checks were green before the exact-head squash merge. No inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was used.
